definition-changed.answer: The rule uses 'procedure division' (the division), never the defined term 'procedure'; §2002:4 (entry 4.150) 'One or more successive paragraphs or sections in the procedure division' vs §2023:3.145 does not touch what the division is. Scope and evidence unchanged.

definition-dropped.answer: §2002:4 (entry 4.121) defines method as a procedural entity of a class definition; 2023 drops the entry and relies on 9.3.4, whose text is word for word §2002:9.3.4. The same source elements are methods in both editions, so the rule governs the same programs. A method prototype is a method definition inside an interface definition (§2002:9.3.6), the same in 2023.

pending-clause.answer: §2002:9.3.5 differs from §2023:9.3.6 only in method RESOLUTION: 2023 adds signature matching and overload steps, 2002 binds by method-name alone. This rule restricts where a name may be written at compile time and does not rest on how an invocation is resolved; scope and evidence unchanged. A method prototype's procedure division holds only its header in both editions; resolution of an invocation against it is not what SR11 governs.
